items.name: Read web pages
items.description: Lets Mav open a link and read the page — to summarise articles, check a recipe, compare offers.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “Summarise this article: <link>”.

items.name: Web browser
items.description: A real browser Mav can drive: click, fill forms, read pages that need JavaScript.
items.note: Downloads a browser the first time it is used (about 150 MB).
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
The first use downloads the browser (about 150 MB), so give it a minute.
Try it: “Open <site>, find the opening hours and tell me”.

items.name: Web search (Brave)
items.description: Private web and news search through the Brave Search API.
steps: Open the Brave Search API page and create a free account.
Subscribe to the free plan (a card may be asked for verification; nothing is charged on the free plan).
In API Keys, create a key and copy it.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Web search (DuckDuckGo)
items.description: Web search with no account and no key — good enough for everyday lookups.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “Search the web for the best-rated bakeries near the Bastille”.
For heavy use, prefer Brave or Tavily: DuckDuckGo may slow down repeated searches.

items.name: Web search (Tavily)
items.description: Search built for AI assistants: fresh results with the page content already extracted.
steps: Sign up at tavily.com (1,000 free searches a month).
Your API key is on the dashboard's home page (it starts with tvly-). Copy it.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Web search (Exa)
items.description: Search by meaning: find companies, people, papers or code that match a description.
steps: Sign up at exa.ai (free credits on sign-up).
Open API Keys in the dashboard and copy your key.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Perplexity
items.description: Ask Perplexity: researched answers with sources, for questions that need several searches.
steps: Sign in at perplexity.ai and open Settings → API.
Add credit (the API is pay-as-you-go), then generate a key.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Web search (Kagi)
items.description: Kagi's ad-free search and its summariser (videos, PDFs, long pages).
steps: You need a Kagi account with API access (the Search API is in closed beta — ask Kagi support for access).
In Settings → API, add API credit and create a token.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Firecrawl
items.description: Turns whole websites into clean text: crawl a site, extract prices or listings, map its pages.
steps: Sign up at firecrawl.dev (free credits each month).
Copy your API key from the dashboard (it starts with fc-).
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Apify
items.description: Thousands of ready-made scrapers: Google Maps reviews, Instagram, Amazon, job boards…
steps: Sign up at apify.com (a monthly free credit is included).
Open Settings → API & Integrations and copy your personal API token.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “Use Apify to get the latest 20 Google reviews of <place>”.

items.name: YouTube transcripts
items.description: Reads the transcript of a YouTube video, to summarise it or find the passage you need.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “Summarise this video in five points: <YouTube link>”.

items.name: Wikipedia
items.description: Search and read Wikipedia articles, with summaries and key facts.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “What does Wikipedia say about the Edict of Nantes?”.

items.name: arXiv papers
items.description: Search scientific papers on arXiv, download them and read them with you.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “Find the three most cited recent papers on battery recycling and summarise them”.

items.name: Zotero
items.description: Your Zotero library: search your references, read notes and annotations.
steps: Sign in at zotero.org and open Settings → Security → Applications.
Create a private key with “Allow library access” (read-only is enough). Copy it.
On the same page, note “Your user ID for use in API calls” (a number).
Paste both below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Context7 (code docs)
items.description: Up-to-date documentation and examples for thousands of programming libraries.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “Using the latest Next.js docs, how do I add a middleware?”.

items.name: DeepWiki
items.description: Ask questions about any public GitHub repository: how it works, where things are.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “Using DeepWiki, how does the opencode project handle sessions?”.

items.name: Microsoft Learn
items.description: Official Microsoft documentation: Azure, Microsoft 365, Windows, .NET, PowerShell.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “How do I set an out-of-office reply for a shared mailbox in Microsoft 365?”.

items.name: AWS documentation
items.description: Search and read the official AWS documentation.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “What are the S3 storage classes and when should I use each?”.

items.name: Cloudflare documentation
items.description: Search the Cloudflare documentation: DNS, Workers, Pages, security settings.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “How do I redirect www to my bare domain on Cloudflare?”.

items.name: Time & time zones
items.description: Current time anywhere and time-zone conversions — handy for calls and trips.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Check your time zone below (it is filled in from your browser). Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Weather
items.description: Forecasts, current conditions, rain and air quality anywhere in the world (Open-Meteo, NOAA).
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “Will it rain in Lyon tomorrow afternoon?”.

items.name: Your files
items.description: Read and organise files in a folder of your server (documents, notes, exports).

inputs.label: Folder Mav may use
inputs.help: Mav can read and write only inside this folder.

steps: Choose the folder Mav may use — Mav cannot see anything outside it.
Type its full path below (for example /home/you/Documents). Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Translation (Lara)
items.description: Professional-grade translation that keeps tone and context, in 200+ languages.
steps: Sign up at laratranslate.com and open the API section of your account (a free plan exists).
Create an access key: you get an Access Key ID and an Access Key Secret.
Paste both below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Google Maps
items.description: Places, addresses, opening hours, travel times and directions.
steps: Open the Google Cloud console and create a project (a billing account is required; Google gives a monthly free credit).
In APIs & Services → Library, enable the Places API, the Geocoding API and the Directions API.
In APIs & Services → Credentials, create an API key, then restrict it to those three APIs.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Flights (Kiwi.com)
items.description: Search flights with flexible dates and get booking links.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “Cheapest return flight Paris → Lisbon, a weekend in March, ±3 days”.

items.name: Notion
items.description: Search, read and update your Notion pages and databases.

inputs.label: Notion integration token
inputs.help: Create an internal integration, then share the pages Mav may use with it.

steps: Open Notion's integrations page and click New integration (type: Internal), name it Mav.
Copy the Internal Integration Secret (it starts with ntn_).
In Notion, open each page Mav may use → ⋯ → Connections → add Mav. Mav sees only those pages.
Paste the secret below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Todoist
items.description: Your tasks and projects: add, reschedule, complete, plan the week.
steps: Nothing to copy: Todoist uses a sign-in.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
On its card in Connections, click Connect, sign in to Todoist and approve, then paste the code (or the whole address) the page shows.
Try it: “Add ‘call the plumber’ to my Todoist for tomorrow 9 am”.

items.name: Linear
items.description: Issues, projects and cycles in Linear: create, update and search.
steps: In Linear, open Settings → Security & access → Personal API keys.
Create a key (Read is enough to only look; add Write to let Mav create issues). Copy it.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: monday.com
items.description: Your monday.com boards and items: read, create and update.
steps: In monday.com, click your avatar → Developers → My access tokens.
Copy your personal token.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Airtable
items.description: Your Airtable bases: search, read, add and update records.
steps: Open Airtable's Builder hub → Personal access tokens → Create token.
Add the scopes data.records:read, data.records:write and schema.bases:read, then pick the bases Mav may use.
Copy the token (it starts with pat). Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Obsidian
items.description: Your Obsidian vault: search, read and write notes.

inputs.label: Obsidian's address
inputs.help: Where Obsidian runs; 127.0.0.1 if on this machine.

steps: In Obsidian, open Settings → Community plugins, install and enable “Local REST API”.
In the plugin's settings, copy the API key.
Obsidian must run on this same machine (or one Mav can reach) and stay open.
Paste the key below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Miro
items.description: Your Miro boards: read sticky notes and diagrams, create new content.
steps: Nothing to copy: Miro uses a sign-in.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
On its card in Connections, click Connect, sign in to Miro and approve, then paste the code (or the whole address) the page shows. Pick the team Mav may use.

items.name: Slack
items.description: Read and post in your Slack channels, reply in threads, look up people.
steps: Open api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → From scratch, and pick your workspace.
In OAuth & Permissions, add the bot scopes channels:history, channels:read, chat:write, reactions:write, users:read.
Click Install to Workspace and copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…).
Your Team ID starts with T: open Slack in a browser, it is in the address (app.slack.com/client/T…/).
Invite the bot to the channels Mav may use (/invite @YourApp). Paste both below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Jira & Confluence (Atlassian Cloud)
items.description: Jira issues and Confluence pages: search, create, update, summarise.
steps: Nothing to copy: Atlassian uses a sign-in.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
On its card in Connections, click Connect, sign in to Atlassian and approve, then paste the code (or the whole address) the page shows. Choose the site Mav may use.
Your site admin may need to allow the “Atlassian Rovo MCP” app first.

items.name: Jira (API token)
items.description: Jira with an API token instead of a sign-in — also works with Jira Server / Data Center.
steps: Open id.atlassian.com → Security → API tokens → Create API token, and copy it.
(Jira Server / Data Center: create a personal access token in your profile instead.)
Fill in your Jira address, your e-mail and the token below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: HubSpot
items.description: Your CRM: contacts, companies, deals and notes.
steps: In HubSpot, open Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → Create a private app (or Development → Legacy apps on newer accounts).
In Scopes, tick the CRM objects Mav may read or write (contacts, companies, deals…).
Create the app and copy its access token (pat-…).
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Intercom
items.description: Customer conversations and contacts in Intercom: search, read, summarise.
steps: Nothing to copy: Intercom uses a sign-in (US-hosted workspaces).
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
On its card in Connections, click Connect, sign in to Intercom and approve, then paste the code (or the whole address) the page shows.

items.name: Canva
items.description: Find, create and export Canva designs.
steps: Nothing to copy: Canva uses a sign-in.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
On its card in Connections, click Connect, sign in to Canva and approve, then paste the code (or the whole address) the page shows.

items.name: Zapier
items.description: 8,000+ apps through Zapier: whatever actions you allow, Mav can run.
steps: Open mcp.zapier.com and create a new MCP server.
Add the actions Mav may run (for example “Google Sheets: add row”).
In Connect, copy the server URL. It contains a secret — keep it private.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Make
items.description: Run your Make scenarios from Mav.
steps: In Make, set the scenarios Mav may run to “On demand” scheduling.
Open your profile → API access → MCP token, and create a token.
Copy the MCP server URL shown with it (it contains the token).
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: n8n
items.description: Call your own n8n workflows as tools.
steps: In n8n, create a workflow that starts with an “MCP Server Trigger” node.
Connect the tools Mav may use to it (other nodes or sub-workflows), then activate the workflow.
Open the trigger node and copy the Production URL.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: GitHub
items.description: Your repositories, issues and pull requests.
steps: Open GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Fine-grained tokens → Generate new token.
Pick the repositories Mav may use and give read (or read and write) access to Contents, Issues and Pull requests.
Copy the token. Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: GitLab
items.description: Your GitLab projects, issues and merge requests.
steps: Type your GitLab address below (https://gitlab.com, or your own instance).
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
On its card in Connections, click Connect, sign in to GitLab and approve, then paste the code (or the whole address) the page shows.
GitLab's MCP server is in beta: on your own instance an administrator may need to turn it on.

items.name: Sentry
items.description: Errors and issues from Sentry: what broke, since when, for whom.
steps: In Sentry, open Settings → Account → API → Personal Tokens → Create New Token.
Give it read access to Organization, Project, Team and Issue & Event. Copy it.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Vercel
items.description: Your Vercel projects and deployments: status, logs, domains.
steps: Nothing to copy: Vercel uses a sign-in.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
On its card in Connections, click Connect, sign in to Vercel and approve, then paste the code (or the whole address) the page shows.

items.name: Netlify
items.description: Your Netlify sites: deploys, forms, environment variables.
steps: In Netlify, open User settings → Applications → Personal access tokens → New access token.
Copy the token. Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Supabase
items.description: One Supabase project, read-only: tables, SQL queries, logs and docs.
steps: In Supabase, open Account → Access Tokens → Generate new token, and copy it (sbp_…).
Open your project → Project Settings → General and copy the Project ID.
Paste both below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Mav connects read-only: it can query, never change your data.

items.name: Neon
items.description: Your Neon Postgres projects: branches, schemas and SQL.
steps: In the Neon console, open Account settings → API keys → Create new API key.
Copy the key. Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Heroku
items.description: Your Heroku apps: status, logs, scaling, add-ons.
steps: Install the Heroku CLI on any computer and run: heroku authorizations:create
(Or Account settings → Applications → Authorizations → Create authorization.)
Copy the token. Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: PostHog
items.description: Product analytics: trends, funnels, feature flags and errors from PostHog.
steps: In PostHog, open Settings → Personal API keys → Create personal API key.
Choose the “MCP Server” preset (or give read access to the data Mav may see). Copy the key.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Hugging Face
items.description: Search models, datasets, papers and Spaces on Hugging Face.
steps: Sign in at huggingface.co and open Settings → Access Tokens → Create new token.
A Read token is enough. Copy it (hf_…).
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.

items.name: Git repository
items.description: A git repository on your server: history, diffs, branches, commits.
steps: Type the full path of the repository below (the folder that contains .git). Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “What changed in this repository this week?”.

items.name: PostgreSQL
items.description: Ask questions of a PostgreSQL database in plain words — read-only.
steps: Ideally, create a read-only user in your database for Mav.
Build its connection string: postgresql://user:password@host:5432/database
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Mav connects in restricted mode: it can read, never change your data.

items.name: MongoDB
items.description: Explore and query a MongoDB database or Atlas cluster — read-only.
steps: In Atlas: Database → Connect → Drivers, copy the connection string and put your password in it.
(Your own server: mongodb://user:password@host:27017/database.)
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Mav connects read-only.

items.name: SQLite database
items.description: Query and analyse a SQLite database file on your server.
steps: Type the full path of the .db / .sqlite file below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Mav can also write to this file: point it at a copy if the data matters.

items.name: Stripe
items.description: Your Stripe account: payments, customers, invoices, subscriptions, refunds.
steps: In the Stripe dashboard, open Developers → API keys → Create restricted key.
Give it only what Mav needs (for example Read on Charges, Customers, Invoices). Copy it (rk_live_… or rk_test_…).
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Start with a test-mode key to try it safely.

items.name: PayPal
items.description: Your PayPal business account: invoices, orders, disputes, transactions.
steps: Nothing to copy: PayPal uses a sign-in (business accounts).
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
On its card in Connections, click Connect, sign in to PayPal and approve, then paste the code (or the whole address) the page shows.

items.name: Square
items.description: Your Square business: payments, orders, catalog, customers.
steps: Nothing to copy: Square uses a sign-in.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
On its card in Connections, click Connect, sign in to Square and approve, then paste the code (or the whole address) the page shows.

items.name: Shopify store
items.description: A Shopify store's catalogue, policies and cart — yours or one you shop at.
steps: Type the store's address below (for example my-shop.myshopify.com or shop.example.com). Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “Which of the store's jackets are waterproof and under €150?”.

items.name: Crypto prices (CoinGecko)
items.description: Live and historical prices, market caps and trends for 15,000+ crypto assets.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Try it: “How did Bitcoin and Ether do this week?”.

items.name: Stock market (Alpha Vantage)
items.description: Stock quotes, company fundamentals, forex and economic indicators.
steps: Request a free API key on Alpha Vantage's site (name and e-mail are enough).
Copy the key. Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
The free tier allows 25 requests a day.

items.name: Stock market (Yahoo Finance)
items.description: Quotes, history, news and financials from Yahoo Finance, with no account.
steps: Nothing to sign up for.
Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
Uses Yahoo Finance's public data (unofficial): fine for personal use, not for trading decisions.

items.name: Home Assistant
items.description: Ask about and control your smart home: lights, heating, sensors.
items.note: Enable the “Model Context Protocol Server” integration in Home Assistant first.
steps: In Home Assistant, open Settings → Devices & services → Add integration → “Model Context Protocol Server”.
Open your profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens → Create token, and copy it.
Fill in Home Assistant's address and the token below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
In the cloud, Mav must be able to reach that address (Nabu Casa or your own public address).

items.name: ElevenLabs voices
items.description: Text to natural speech, voice cloning and transcription with ElevenLabs.
steps: Sign up at elevenlabs.io (a free monthly quota is included).
Open Developers → API Keys → Create API key, and copy it.
Paste it below. Click Add, then Apply changes when Mav asks.
